# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 2 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus (ch 1-31) / P.Mich. 130 (ch 32+), Shepherd of Hermas 2 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_002_page_001.jpg

---

## Vision 1, Chapter 2

**1** After saying this she went silent and disappeared. I was shaking and grief-stricken. I thought to myself: "If even that thought is held against me, how can there be any hope for me? I've committed so many serious sins — how do I make that right with God? What words could I possibly find to ask for his mercy?" **2** While I was going back and forth over all this, a large white chair appeared in front of me, made of brilliant white wool. An elderly woman came and sat down in it, dressed in shining robes, with a book in her hands. She looked at me and said: "Hello, Hermas!" **3** I was so upset I could barely respond. "Hello, my lady," I said through tears. She asked, "Why so sad, Hermas? You're such a patient, gentle person — you usually have a smile on your face. Why are you looking so downcast today?" **4** "It's because of a good woman," I said, "who tells me I've sinned against her." "Nonsense," she replied. "A servant of God doesn't behave like that! But it's true that the thought crossed your heart — and that's exactly how sin gets a foothold in God's servants. An evil intention is ruinous, especially in someone upright — and doubly so in someone like you, Hermas, who is known for your self-control and your avoidance of evil desires." **5** "But God's displeasure with you isn't only about that. It's also because you've failed to discipline your household. Your family has been sinning against God and against you, their own parent. You love your children — but love without correction does no good. You let your household fall into serious corruption and did nothing about it. That's why God is displeased with you. But he will set all of this right; he will undo the damage your family has done. The worry and strain you've felt — that came from their sins and failures. **6** Yet God's great mercy has looked on you and your family with compassion. He will rebuild you and establish you in his glory. Don't drag your feet — take courage, and get to work rebuilding your household. A blacksmith beats his metal into shape through repeated blows; in the same way, practicing righteousness every day hammers wickedness into submission. Keep correcting your children — don't give up on them. I know that if they turn back to God with all their hearts, they will be written into the book of life alongside all the saints."

---

*PNEUMA note: The "book of life" connection anticipates Revelation's imagery; the blacksmith simile is made more vivid for contemporary readers.*
